caption: Your idea is often judged by ROI alone. This carousel adds a structured, scenario-based evaluation you can reuse. Which criterion do you trust most when evaluating a new idea? #AI #DecisionMaking #Productivity #Entrepreneurs

slides.title: Your decision metric is insufficient
slides.body: Your decision metric is insufficient. Five prompts test reliability, bias, and depth.

slides.title: 1. Diagnose weakness
slides.body: Diagnose weakness: Identify three blind spots in evaluating an idea using ROI only. Input: [IDEA]. Output: bullets with brief explanations.

slides.title: 2. Define criteria
slides.body: Define criteria: Propose complete decision criteria for [IDEA] across impact, feasibility, risk, timing, and ethics.

slides.title: 3. Quantify risks
slides.body: Quantify risks: Rate each criterion 1–5, estimate likelihood, and give worst/best-case outcomes.

slides.title: 4. Scenario planning
slides.body: Scenario planning: Create base, optimistic, and pessimistic scenarios for [IDEA], scoring per criterion.

slides.title: 5. Create workflow
slides.body: Create workflow: Provide a reusable fill-in checklist for any idea, with owner, due date, and next steps.

slides.title: Takeaway
slides.body: Takeaway: Use multi-criteria thinking and scenarios to defend decisions, not rely on one metric.
